title: Territory-aware fallback ruleset and tenant permitlist for EU data-residency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a territory-aware routing ruleset and tenant-level permitlist and denylist to enforce EU-only data residency for requests that require it. This ticket covers the runtime decision path (Policy Decision Service), the gateway enforcement hooks, and the model-variant fallback chain for cases where EU-local capacity or compatible variants are unavailable. Goal: deterministic, auditable routing that prevents egress to non-EU regions for qualified tenants while providing controlled fallbacks and emergency overrides.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a compact Policy DSL (JSON/YAML) that declares per-tenant residency requirements, permitted regions, and ordered fallback model variants. 2) Extend the Routing Decision Service (RDS) with a Residency module that evaluates tenant attributes, request metadata, and current capacity signals to produce a concrete routing plan. 3) Add an enforcement hook at the edge/gateway that rejects or rewrites requests that would violate residency constraints; the hook logs decisions to an audit stream. 4) Implement fallback chains that prefer EU-resident model variants, then EU-edge-compatible containerized variants, then a final controlled-deny option (hard-block) or emergency-pass with audit and async encryption measures. 5) Expose tenant permitlist/denylist management APIs in the Console and a vetted backfill import for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Residency Policy DSL defined with examples and schema published in Confluence
RDS Residency module returns a routing decision that includes: target_region, model_variant_chain, enforcement_action
Gateway enforces hard-block for tenant requests that are marked EU-residency and would route to non-EU targets; a clear audit event emitted
Fallback chain selects EU-local variant when available; when not available, selects next variant in chain and marks the decision reason
Tenant permitlist and denylist can be configured via Console and via API; changes are reflected within 60s in routing decisions
End-to-end e2e tests cover blocked, allowed, and fallback flows; unit tests for decision logic with >=90% coverage
Telemetry dashboards show per-tenant residency violations, fallback frequency, and egress volume by region
Security review completed and sign-off obtained from Security and Legal
technical_notes:
Feature flags: rds.residency_v1 (default off), gateway.residency_enforce (default off). Example policy snippet:

policy_version: 1
tenant_id: t-12345
residency: EU_ONLY
allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
model_preferences: [redwood-7B-eu-q8, redwood-7B-eu-q4, redwood-7B-global-q4]

RDS will evaluate: tenant metadata -> request headers (X-tenant-region-preference) -> live capacity hints -> policy to produce ordered target list and enforcement_action (ALLOW/FALLBACK/BLOCK/ESCALATE). Gateways will reject with 403 and audit.reason = "residency_block" when action is BLOCK. All decisions include decision_id for trace correlation.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge policy DSL and RDS residency module behind feature flag; unit tests and integration harness. 2) Canary: enable for internal staging tenant set and 5% of EU tenants with monitoring. 3) Expand to 25% after 72h if no regression in fallback rates, latency, or egress. 4) Enable gateway enforcement for canary tenants with hard-block disabled (log-only) for 48h, then enable hard-block for opted tenants. 5) Complete Console UI + API and enable full enforcement for tenants that requested EU-only residency. Rollback is immediate feature-flag off; emergency override endpoint gated to SRE with audit trail.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased latency from an extra decision hop in RDS. Mitigation: cache recent decisions (TTL 15s) and precompute for high-throughput tenants.\nRisk: False-blocking customers due to stale capacity signals. Mitigation: conservative default behavior is FALLBACK-to-compatible EU-edge variants or soft-deny (log-only) for first hour after change; operator alerting.\nRisk: Complex policy precedence causing unexpected routing. Mitigation: canonical precedence doc + validation in Console + a dry-run mode that reports differences before enforcement.
qa_plan: Automated unit tests for Policy DSL parser and decision logic
Integration tests in staging with simulated capacity loss and variant unavailability
Manual QA of Console permitlist/denylist flows and API endpoints
Chaos test: simulate EU region outage and verify fallback chain behavior and audit logs
Load test to verify decision cache prevents P95 latency regression > 20ms
